_why:
Twenty-nine edges into the waived-SAP notification group, every one of which already carried a precise note and none of which carried a source. This attaches the statute the notes rest on rather than rewriting them: 10 U.S.C. 119, read from the Office of Law Revision Counsel text on 22 August 2026, subsection (e)(2) for who is notified and (g) for which bodies count.

Where an edge turns on whether a person holds one of the twelve seats, the Senate's table of session convening dates is added too, because that is what dates the seat. Where it turns on the contrast with the Gang of Eight - Reid and McConnell - 50 U.S.C. 3093(c)(2) is added, since the point of those edges is that the two groups are disjoint sets: 3093 includes the majority and minority leaders of the Senate and 119(g) does not.

The structural fact these edges collectively carry is worth stating plainly, because it is not obvious and it is fully documented: the House Oversight Committee, which took the July 2023 Grusch testimony and has driven the public record since, is NOT one of the six bodies named in 10 U.S.C. 119(g). It holds no entitlement under (e)(2) and no statutory route to compel waived-SAP material. Neither do the party leaders. The committees that could be told are not the committees that have been asking.
